key_insight: Replacing Cr with Cu in MnFeCoNi HEAs significantly improves bifunctional alkaline water electrolysis performance by tuning surface chemistry and intermediate binding.
engineering_relevance: A single-element substitution offers a practical design lever for creating lower-overpotential, cost-effective HEA electrocatalysts for hydrogen and oxygen evolution.
method: Compared CrMnFeCoNi (HEA-Cr) vs MnFeCoNiCu (HEA-Cu) under identical alkaline HER and OER conditions.
Combined electrochemical testing with computational analysis of binding energies for H*, O*, OH*, and OOH*.
Examined post-OER surface reconstruction to assess elemental migration and active-layer formation.
evidence_signal: HEA-Cu outperformed HEA-Cr, reaching 538 mV overpotential and a 165 mV dec⁻¹ Tafel slope, with calculations supporting more favorable reaction-intermediate binding.
watch_item: Post-OER Cu migration forms a Cu-rich outer shell, so durability and surface reconstruction under long-term operation need careful validation.
paper_title: Structure-Property Correlation of Cr/Cu-MnFeCoNi High-Entropy Alloys for Alkaline Water Electrolysis
